title: Cosmic fireworks over Paranal
caption: The Milky Way over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The arc of the Milky Way dominates this panorama over ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT), its bright band laced with dark filaments of dust that absorb and hide the light of stars behind them, and dotted with bright patches where new stars are forming. Just below the arc hang the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, two small galactic neighbors, above two of the VLT's 1.8-meter Auxiliary Telescopes.

On the right, beyond the row of four 8.2-meter Unit Telescopes that make up the VLT, faint red and green airglow lights the sky above the horizon. Zodiacal light adds its own diffuse glow, produced by microscopic grains of dust scattering light in the plane of the Solar System.

The VLT sits 2635 meters above sea level at Paranal Observatory in northern Chile. Pictures like this, taken by ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek, show why telescopes are placed in such remote spots, and how richly the long trip there is rewarded.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based panoramic photograph by Petr Horálek. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: Airglow and zodiacal light are faint, and a camera gathering light over time may show their colors and glow more clearly than the eye.

alt: The Milky Way arching over a line of four large telescope enclosures and two small domes, with two fuzzy patches below the arc and faint red and green glows near the horizon.
